title: Do you lose the right to privacy when you die?
summary: Josh and Chuck explore whether people keep any privacy rights after death. They open with the DeathSwitch service, which sends scheduled emails after a user stops responding, then survey U.S. privacy rights for the living (Constitution, Ninth/Fourth/Fourteenth Amendments, Meyer v. Nebraska, Griswold, Lawrence v. Texas, the Privacy Act of 1974, HIPAA). They explain that the Privacy Act ends at death while HIPAA extends to family, and cover the right of publicity (Einstein's estate, CMG Worldwide, Elvis, Marilyn Monroe, Fred Astaire's Dirt Devil ad) and state variation. They discuss FOIA and withheld death photos (Vince Foster, Dale Earnhardt), the News of the World phone-hacking scandal involving Milly Dowler, posthumous defamation, and Facebook memorial accounts. The episode closes with a listener mail about a former cult member's uncle leaving a group after listening to the show's cult episode.
topics: News of the World phone hacking

segments.title: Opening banter and DeathSwitch
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the topic of privacy after death and describe the DeathSwitch service, which sends preset emails if a user fails to respond to periodic check-ins.

segments.title: Privacy rights of the living under the Constitution
segments.summary: They discuss how the Supreme Court has interpreted the Constitution, including the Ninth, Fourth and Fourteenth Amendments, to recognize privacy rights, citing Meyer v. Nebraska, Griswold v. Connecticut, and Lawrence v. Texas.

segments.title: Privacy Act of 1974 and HIPAA
segments.summary: The hosts explain the Federal Privacy Act of 1974, which governs federal records and ends at death, and HIPAA, which covers medical information and extends rights to family after death.

segments.title: Right of publicity and descendible rights
segments.summary: The right of publicity is described as originating with 1950s baseball cards, now allowing estates to control and license celebrity likeness. Examples include Einstein's estate, CMG Worldwide, the Fred Astaire Dirt Devil ad, and wigs of dead celebrities.

segments.title: State variation, Marilyn Monroe and FOIA death photos
segments.summary: They note that publicity rights vary by state, with Tennessee, Washington and Indiana allowing posthumous rights, and discuss Marilyn Monroe's estate and FOIA rules that often keep autopsy and crime scene photos from release, including the Vince Foster and Dale Earnhardt cases.

segments.title: News of the World phone hacking and posthumous defamation
segments.summary: The hosts describe News of the World hacking the voicemail of murdered schoolgirl Milly Dowler, deleting messages, and the resulting closure of the paper. They then discuss whether crimes and defamation can harm the dead, including California's anti-defamation approach.
topics: News of the World phone hacking

segments.title: Facebook accounts after death
segments.summary: Chuck describes finding a former friend's Facebook page turned memorial after her death, and the hosts discuss Facebook's policy of converting inactive accounts to memorial pages.

segments.title: Sponsor read and show plugs
segments.summary: Plugs for the Stuff to Blow Your Mind podcast, the article on privacy after death, and a sponsor read for the Toyota Camry.

segments.title: Listener mail: cult story
segments.summary: A listener writes that after hearing the show's cult episode, their uncle left a polygamous group that had ordered his fourteen-year-old daughter to marry a group member.
